decisions.finding_quote: a 300 s budget timeout while waiting for a model response (HA-COMPRESS run-003)
decisions.reason: I read the run-003 trajectory (mini-swe-agent.traj.json) and commands.log, which puts the timer start at 12:16:12.221Z. The single assistant message is at +5.49 s and carries 3 tool calls (grep, defects4j test, find). All three tool results are stamped +304.85 s, after which the run exits with TimeExceeded. model_stats.api_calls is 1, and block_mxF0.jsonl also has api_calls 1. Runs 001 and 004 to 006 of the same variant got their first tool results 0.06 to 0.57 s after the model response. The budget therefore ran out in the tool step, not while waiting on the model. X11's 'second model call did not return' is not supported either. Edits B and M fix the report.

decisions.finding_quote: held-out confirmation is complete for the 3 strongest
decisions.reason: The problem is real. family_summary.json lists M19 (0.0), M5 (0.5) and M3 (0.714) as the only PROMISING families, and M10 as NULL (3/3). The held-out keys are M10 (HA), M19 (HB) and M3 (HC). The frozen plan does derive the HA, HB and HC failure modes from those three families' S1 misses and states stop rule B on that basis, so the report follows the plan's operationalisation. It should say so explicitly. One part of the proposed fix is wrong: it says M5 was represented through HA and HC. The plan table assigns MASK-01 and CF-V1 to HA, and MASK-01 run 3 to HB, so M5 is carried through HA and HB, not HC. Edit C also absorbs the n = 4 point and the 'robust' scope.

edits.new:
The global stop rule's condition **B** is met, as the frozen held-out plan operationalises it:

- 17 families were screened, against a requirement of at least 12;
- held-out confirmation is complete for three failure-mode recipes (HA, HB, HC) that the plan derived from the S1 misses of
  the three strongest screened families (M19, M3, M5). The recipes are coded M10, M19 and M3: M5 is carried only through the
  HA and HB failure modes, and M10 itself screened NULL (NEW-R7-M10, 3/3). One HB cell, HO-HB-COMPRESS-01, has 4 valid runs
  rather than the preregistered 5 (X11);
- none reaches pooled Acc@1 ≤ 0.60.

Under rule B's preregistered wording, GPT-5.6 is therefore robust under the tested manipulations. This is scoped to GPT-5.6 at
effort medium in mini-swe-agent (300 s) on these 9 synthetic single-fault instances, and the per-recipe Wilson 95% lower
bounds (0.702, 0.785, 0.796) do not exclude moderate reductions.

decisions.finding_quote: no mechanism reduces GPT-5.6's accuracy on fresh held-out instances.
decisions.reason: I recomputed the Wilson 95% intervals: 14/15 gives (0.702, 0.988), 14/14 gives (0.785, 1.0) and 15/15 gives (0.796, 1.0). HA's lower bound is below X8's 0.80 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED threshold, so the headline overclaims. What the data show is that no recipe reached ≤ 0.60. The proposed phrase 'reductions of up to about 20 to 30 points' assumes a baseline that the held-out design lacks, so I instead name the lower bounds directly. 'Robust under the tested manipulations' is the preregistered rule-B wording, so I keep it, with scope and the intervals added (edit C).

edits.new: **Result: none of the three held-out recipes brought GPT-5.6's pooled Acc@1 down to the preregistered ≤ 0.60 threshold on fresh held-out instances.**

decisions.reason: P4-DEPTH-01-r1/spec.json has two edits: the NumberUtils.overlay decoy javadoc, and BitField.widen's javadoc changed to unsigned words, with why 'pin the gold's contract'. P4-COMPRESS07-r1 removes TarBuffer.digest and TarBufferTest.java. Both scored 3/3 against 0/3 for their parents. The two-sided Fisher p for [[0,3],[3,0]] is 0.10. X4 says revisions are 'never confirmation evidence'. The causal framing and the single-edit attribution for DEPTH-01 are therefore overclaims. Edit K also covers the next finding.

edits.old:
The Phase 4 diagnostics had already shown why. The two 0/3 screening effects vanished, 3/3 each, once the decoy's doc
contradiction was removed (DEPTH-01) and the correct sibling offering an alternative entry-point repair was removed
(COMPRESS-07). Held-out instances that leave the documentation a single defensible owner reproduce that ceiling.
edits.new:
The Phase 4 diagnostics are consistent with this, but they are exploratory (X4) and small. The two 0/3 screening effects
became 3/3 each after validity repairs (n = 3 per arm; 0/3 against 3/3 gives a two-sided Fisher p of 0.10). The DEPTH-01
revision made two javadoc edits, removing the decoy's doc contradiction and pinning the gold's own contract, so which edit
mattered is not identified. The COMPRESS-07 revision removed the correct sibling that offered an alternative entry-point
repair, together with its test. The held-out instances, whose documentation makes the gold the single defensible owner, were
also at or near ceiling. No held-out arm varied that property, and 8 of the 9 builder reports had already flagged the gold as
easy to spot or the instance as at ceiling risk. The held-out null therefore cannot be credited specifically to single-owner
documentation, and it does not show robustness to stronger forms of these mechanisms.

decisions.finding_quote: Odd-looking correct code alone does not mislead when nearby evidence pins it (M1, M3 with a pinned definer).
decisions.reason: DEFINER-01 is a clean counterexample. Run-001 ranked PlotUtilities::drift first (gold rank 5), and the blind label states that drift is pinned by PlotUtilitiesTests::testDrift. CHART-01-ADAPTER is weaker evidence. Its misses blamed the caller CompassPlot::ring, not an odd-looking definer, and the coordinator judged those answers defensible, so that case is contested. The item-3 rewrite (edit given under finding 1) cites DEFINER-01 as the counterexample, marks CHART-01-ADAPTER as contested, and limits the protective claim to the two S2 prototypes.

decisions.reason: The SCREENING_BUILD_RECIPES.md table has no M5 recipe; M6 is folded into R1 with M1, and R1 provides no sibling, inverse or second caller. In family_summary.json, M5 is family_class PROMISING (3/6), not a failed mechanism. R3 (M3) does provide a passing test and a second production caller: NEW-R3-M3's builder report cites PoissonDistribution.probability. So M3 belongs in the list, which finding 21's version leaves out. I also checked the evidence chains of the NULL runs. M2 (CTV-72D9FC) cites the writer in all 3 runs and readNewEntry in 2. M7 (CTV-31B7B9) cites the encoder in all 3. M8 (CTV-50035B) never displays the bodies of the second callers. The edit lists the right recipes, reports the observed comparisons modestly, and adds the held-out construction caveat (finding 24).

edits.old:
The agent compares the gold with its sibling, its inverse or its second caller, which
   recipes M2, M5 to M8 and M17 deliberately provide so that the task stays solvable.
edits.new:
The S2 recipes for M2, M3, M7, M8 and M17 deliberately provide decisive evidence of this kind (a sibling, an inverse, a
   second caller or a passing test) so that the task stays solvable. The correct runs were not systematically coded. In the

decisions.finding_quote: The Phase 4 diagnostics explain why the screening effects did not transfer
decisions.reason: MECHANISM_SCREENING_MATRIX.csv has P4 rows only for P4-DEPTH-01-r1 and P4-COMPRESS07-r1 (3/3 each). P4-DEPTH-01-r1's spec has two javadoc edits, so its recovery is confounded, as PROMISING_MECHANISMS.md concedes. AMENDMENTS X4 says revisions are never confirmation evidence. MASK-01, CHART-01-ADAPTER, DEFINER-01 and CF-V1 were never revised. A causal 'explain' is therefore not supported. The edit also covers finding 18.

edits.old:
The Phase 4 diagnostics explain why the screening effects did not transfer: the two 0/3 effects became 3/3 once the validity
problem was repaired (PROMISING_MECHANISMS.md).
edits.new:
Phase 4 (exploratory, n = 3 per arm, AMENDMENTS X4) revised only the two 0/3 instances, and both became 3/3 after their
flagged features were changed. P4-COMPRESS07-r1 removed the correct sibling; P4-DEPTH-01-r1 changed two javadocs at once (the
decoy's contradiction and the gold's contract), so its two repairs are not separable. This is consistent with, but does not
establish, those two effects depending on validity problems. The other reductions (MASK-01 1/3, CHART-01-ADAPTER 1/3,
